theater.title: Iran war
theater.sub: The options the US has right now in the Iran war, and what followed the last times the US did something like each one.
theater.proxy_note: An Iran-backed group is a militia Iran arms in Iraq or Syria. Before 2026, Iran mostly answered the US through these groups; those replies count.
theater.hold_note: Hold cases are weeks of the 2026 war with no logged US sanctions, naval, strike or posture move (Feb 28-Apr 7 and Jul 7-25 left out: US activity there was continuous but logged as a few rows; pre-war weeks left out: too sparsely logged). Most hold weeks have few or no logged events, so they show what the log records in quiet weeks.
theater.not_measured: Oil prices, strain with allies and harm to ordinary Iranians are not measured.
theater.under_logged: The log is a sample. It starts at the Nov 1979 embassy takeover, but 1981-86, 1988-94, 1997-2001, 2003-05 and 2008-09 are thinly logged: before 2019 it holds the big crises, sanctions rounds, UN votes and talks, not every incident, and the Tanker War is logged as a few key clashes. Many pre-1990 rows rest on Washington Post archive pages. Some stretches are logged as one row (for example the nightly US strikes of Jul 9-25, 2026), so "none logged" is not proof nothing happened.

risks: Ship crews: attacks on shipping continue at ~3.5 a week (e.g. On Peace, Oct 6: 12 crew injured). No new US act to answer.
No new US trigger. Iranian or unidentified attacks on shipping keep happening anyway (baseline). Whether holding back changes Iran's behaviour: not measured.
No added interceptor use from a US act; the blockade and patrols continue to cost what they cost now (not measured).
Baseline: ~3.5 attacks on shipping a week in the current phase. Oil prices and shipping costs: not measured.

Iran rejected the US counter-offer (#144, Nov 3; #166, Nov 10). Trump's no-strike pledge ran to Nov 3; limited US strikes on Qeshm came on Nov 2, Nov 6 and Nov 17 (#142, #149, #179). Strain with allies: not measured.
options.pros: No new US act for Iran to answer, so no added risk of retaliation from it. Trump's pledge of no strikes before Nov 3 has passed; limited US strikes on Qeshm came on Nov 2, Nov 6 and Nov 17 (#142, #149, #179). Iran rejected the US counter-offer (#144, Nov 3; #166, Nov 10). Uses no interceptors.
options.harms: Attacks on shipping continue at the baseline rate shown above, injuring crews (On Peace: 12 hurt) and raising shipping risk. Whether holding back weakens deterrence cannot be measured from this log.
options.unknown: Shipping attacks have kept coming without any new US move (see the baseline line). Trump said there would be no US strikes before Nov 3; that date has passed. Limited US strikes on Qeshm Island followed on Nov 2, Nov 6 and Nov 17 (#142, #149, #179), and Iran's security chief Rezaei called the US response 'not convincing' (#144, Nov 3) and told the US to 'fold your hand' (#166). What Iran does next is not in the data.
